metadata.title: Activity-related knee pain after repeated jumping
metadata.description: A curated educational map comparing exposure-related patellar-tendon, local-load, and patellofemoral mechanism families without diagnosing a condition.
metadata.educational_notice: Curated and educational, not comprehensive. Mechanical loading, tissue adaptation, diagnoses, nociception, and reported pain are not treated as interchangeable.
example_questions: What biological mechanisms could contribute to knee pain after repeated jumping?
Why might my knee hurt after basketball jumping?

context_defaults.symptom_or_process: pain during or after repeated jumping or landing
context_defaults.tissue: patellar tendon and patellofemoral structures considered as competing contexts
context_defaults.population: general research context; not an individual diagnosis
important_uncertainty: Pain location and provoking tasks do not identify one anatomical diagnosis.
Mechanical load, tissue adaptation, pain sensitivity, and clinical symptoms are distinct constructs.

metadata.interpreted_summary: We interpreted this as an educational mechanism question about activity-related knee pain after repeated jumping, not as a diagnosis of patellar tendinopathy or patellofemoral pain.

numerical_data.explanation: No approved numerical observations, identified unknown parameters, priors, likelihood, or identifiability review are included in this educational pack.

entities.name: Repeated jumping
entities.description: Repeated jump and landing exposures; frequency, intensity, history, and recovery context are separate variables.

entities.name: Weekly volleyball exposure
entities.description: Training hours and match sets used as exposure proxies in a prospective youth-volleyball cohort.

entities.name: Landing mechanics
entities.description: Observable movement and velocity features during landing; they do not identify tissue pathology.

entities.name: Estimated patellar-tendon force
entities.description: Model-estimated tendon force and loading rate, not a direct in-vivo force measurement.

entities.name: Local patellar-tendon stress state
entities.description: A model-level tissue stress construct that is neither measured damage nor a diagnosis.

entities.name: Tendon mechanical-property adaptation
entities.description: Changes in stiffness, Young’s modulus, or cross-sectional area after chronic loading; these properties are not equivalent to pain relief.

entities.name: Recovery capacity
entities.description: An explicitly latent systems-model construct representing recovery processes; no bundled study directly measures it as one variable.

entities.name: Clinically identified patellar tendinopathy
entities.description: A clinical research population kept distinct from undifferentiated activity-related knee pain.

entities.name: Nociceptive signaling state
entities.description: A model-level signaling process related to threat and pain processing; it is not directly measured by the bundled clinical trials.

entities.name: Activity-related knee pain
entities.description: Pain during or after activity, which can arise from multiple tissues and mechanisms and cannot determine a diagnosis by itself.

entities.name: Force-distribution capacity
entities.description: An abstract biomechanical capacity concept involving strength and movement, not a directly validated diagnostic metric.

entities.name: Patellofemoral mechanical load
entities.description: Mechanical loading at the patellofemoral joint, represented as a competing anatomical branch.

entities.name: Patellofemoral pain population
entities.description: A clinical anterior-knee-pain population distinct from patellar tendinopathy.

entities.name: Progressive tendon-loading program
entities.description: A staged rehabilitation program evaluated in people with confirmed patellar tendinopathy.

entities.name: Isometric exercise
entities.description: Static muscle loading studied for tendinopathy pain, with variable responses and no established universal superiority.

entities.name: Acute pain response
entities.description: Short-term change in reported pain, kept distinct from tissue adaptation or structural healing.

entities.name: Education plus supervised exercise
entities.description: A combined program studied in adolescents with patellofemoral pain, not patellar tendinopathy.

entities.name: Self-reported recovery
entities.description: Participant-reported recovery outcome in a clinical trial; not a molecular or structural measure.

entities.name: Inflammatory-mediator state
entities.description: An abstract state in the educational Petri model; no biomarker inference is made for an individual.

evidence.title: Predicting the patellar tendon force generated when landing from a jump

population.description: 50 skilled or highly skilled volleyball players performing a lateral stop-jump

effect_estimate.measure: variance in estimated tendon loading rate explained by regression model
effect_estimate.source_note: The reported model explained 70% of loading-rate variance; this is not a causal effect size.

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Peak-force and loading-rate regression models explained 52% and 70% of estimated variance, respectively.
limitations: Tendon force was estimated rather than directly measured.
Cross-sectional modeling cannot establish future pain or tendinopathy causation.
Volleyball landing context may not generalize to every activity.
evidence.evidence_note: Quadriceps strength and selected landing velocities contributed to models of estimated peak patellar-tendon force and loading rate during a stop-jump.

evidence.title: Human tendon adaptation in response to mechanical loading: a systematic review and meta-analysis of exercise intervention studies on healthy adults

population.description: 27 longitudinal studies, 37 interventions, and 264 healthy adults with patellar or Achilles-tendon outcomes

context.temporal_context: exercise interventions lasting at least eight weeks

effect_estimate.measure: standardized mean difference in tendon stiffness
effect_estimate.source_note: Meta-analytic effect across included human loading interventions.

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Stiffness SMD 0.70 (95% CI 0.51–0.88); Young’s modulus 0.69 (0.36–1.03); cross-sectional area 0.24 (0.07–0.42).
limitations: Healthy tendons only.
Patellar and Achilles studies were synthesized together.
Mechanical properties are not synonymous with capacity, tissue health, injury prevention, or pain relief.
evidence.evidence_note: Longitudinal loading interventions in healthy adults were associated with increases in tendon stiffness, Young’s modulus, and smaller changes in cross-sectional area.

evidence.title: Training volume and body composition as risk factors for developing jumper's knee among young elite volleyball players
evidence.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports

population.description: 141 initially healthy elite volleyball players followed prospectively; 28 developed clinically diagnosed jumper’s knee

effect_estimate.measure: odds ratio per additional weekly training hour
effect_estimate.source_note: Longitudinal association; not a causal effect or universal threshold.

evidence.uncertainty_measure: OR 1.72 (95% CI 1.18–2.53) per additional training hour and OR 3.88 (1.80–8.40) per additional match set per week.
limitations: Hours and match sets are exposure proxies, not direct tendon-load measurements.
Residual confounding is possible.
No universal load-to-capacity threshold was tested.
evidence.evidence_note: Greater volleyball training and match exposure were longitudinally associated with incident clinically identified jumper’s knee in this youth elite cohort.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of isometric exercise in the management of tendinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials

population.description: 10 randomized studies across patellar, rotator-cuff, lateral-elbow, Achilles, and gluteal tendinopathy

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Limited evidence found no superiority over isotonic exercise immediately or through 12 weeks; responses varied.
limitations: Only three included studies were rated good quality.
Heterogeneous tendon sites and protocols.
Pain response does not measure peripheral nociception or structural healing.
evidence.evidence_note: Isometric exercise produced variable pain responses and was not consistently superior to isotonic exercise in the limited randomized evidence.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of progressive tendon-loading exercise therapy in patients with patellar tendinopathy: a randomised clinical trial

population.description: 76 people with clinical and ultrasound-confirmed, mostly chronic patellar tendinopathy

effect_estimate.measure: adjusted between-group difference in VISA-P improvement
effect_estimate.source_note: Progressive loading versus pain-provoking eccentric-only therapy at 24 weeks.

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Return-to-sport difference was not statistically significant (43% versus 27%, p=0.13).
limitations: Both groups received education, activity-modification advice, and ancillary exercise.
Adherence was low.
A statistically significant contrast is not automatically clinically important or universal.
evidence.evidence_note: A progressive loading program produced greater mean VISA-P improvement than a pain-provoking eccentric-only program at 24 weeks in this patellar-tendinopathy trial.

evidence.title: Exercise during school hours when added to patient education improves outcome for 2 years in adolescent patellofemoral pain: a cluster randomised trial

population.description: 121 adolescents with patellofemoral pain in a cluster-randomized trial

effect_estimate.measure: odds ratio for self-reported recovery at 12 months
effect_estimate.source_note: Education plus supervised exercise relative to education alone.

evidence.uncertainty_measure: The reported number needed to treat was 11 at 12 months and 5 at 24 months.
limitations: Patellofemoral pain is not patellar tendinopathy.
Estimates adding exercise to education, not education alone.
Does not isolate one biological mediator.
evidence.evidence_note: Adding supervised school-based exercise to education increased self-reported recovery relative to education alone in adolescents with patellofemoral pain.

assertions.subject: repeated_jumping
assertions.interpretation: Repeated training and match participation increase measured weekly exposure; jump count and tendon force were not directly measured.
limitations: Volleyball hours are only a proxy for repeated jumping and loading.

assertions.subject: volleyball_exposure
assertions.interpretation: Greater weekly exposure was associated with incident clinically diagnosed jumper’s knee.
limitations: Residual confounding remains possible; this is not a universal threshold.

assertions.subject: patellar_tendinopathy
assertions.interpretation: The trial population had symptomatic patellar tendinopathy and activity-related limitations; this association does not diagnose the cause of an arbitrary knee-pain query.
limitations: Clinical selection context cannot identify pathology from symptoms alone.

assertions.subject: repeated_jumping
assertions.interpretation: Jump performance includes a landing phase with measurable movement features.
limitations: Does not identify a pathological movement pattern.

assertions.subject: landing_mechanics
assertions.interpretation: Selected landing velocities and strength measures contributed to regression estimates of tendon force and loading rate.
limitations: Force was estimated, not directly measured; no pain outcome was studied.

assertions.subject: estimated_tendon_force
assertions.interpretation: Estimated force is represented as a mechanical input to a tissue-stress state; neither source directly measured this state during painful activity.
limitations: Model bridge; mechanical stress must not be equated with tissue damage.

assertions.subject: local_tendon_stress
assertions.interpretation: A tissue-stress-to-pain link is plausible in a patellar-tendinopathy context but was not directly identified by the cited clinical trial.
limitations: Pain is multifactorial; no direct stress or nociceptor measurement is bundled.

assertions.subject: estimated_tendon_force

context.temporal_context: acute force estimate projected onto chronic adaptation

assertions.interpretation: This is a model bridge from an estimated single-jump force to chronic tendon adaptation. The cited review tested loading interventions over at least eight weeks, not this acute-force endpoint.
limitations: The source does not establish that a single-jump force estimate causes chronic adaptation.
Healthy-adult tendon adaptation does not imply pain relief, healing, or prevention.

assertions.subject: tendon_adaptation
assertions.interpretation: The Petri model treats adaptation as a modifier of stress accumulation, but the meta-analysis did not test this mediation or pain.
limitations: Explicit modeling assumption.

assertions.subject: recovery_capacity
assertions.interpretation: Recovery capacity is a latent model construct proposed to modify accumulated stress; it was not directly measured as one quantity.
limitations: No validated numeric load-to-capacity ratio or threshold.

assertions.subject: local_tendon_stress
assertions.interpretation: The model proposes a stress-to-nociceptive-state bridge, but the cited pain review did not measure peripheral signaling.
limitations: Unvalidated mechanistic bridge.

assertions.subject: nociceptive_signaling
assertions.interpretation: Nociceptive processing can contribute to pain, but reported pain responses do not directly measure this modeled state.
limitations: Pain is not a direct readout of a single peripheral signal.

assertions.subject: force_distribution
assertions.interpretation: Force distribution may change local joint loading, but the cited tendon-force study did not estimate patellofemoral load.
limitations: Cross-anatomical extrapolation retained as a weak link.

assertions.subject: patellofemoral_load
assertions.interpretation: Mechanical loading is a plausible context modifier, but the clinical trial did not identify load as the cause of pain.
limitations: No causal load estimate in the cited trial.

assertions.subject: patellofemoral_pain
assertions.interpretation: Patellofemoral pain is retained as a distinct clinical population that can present with activity-related pain.
limitations: Does not imply a diagnosis for a user’s symptom.

assertions.subject: progressive_loading
assertions.interpretation: The progressive program improved a validated clinical score more than a pain-provoking eccentric-only comparator at 24 weeks.
limitations: Combined program; low adherence; no individual recommendation.

assertions.subject: isometric_exercise
assertions.interpretation: Randomized evidence showed variable acute pain responses and no consistent superiority over isotonic exercise.
limitations: Acute analgesia is not structural healing.

assertions.subject: education_exercise
assertions.interpretation: Adding supervised exercise to education increased self-reported recovery relative to education alone in this distinct population.
limitations: Not evidence for patellar tendinopathy or education alone.

hypotheses.title: Exposure-associated patellar-tendon pathway
hypotheses.summary: Higher weekly volleyball exposure was prospectively associated with incident jumper’s knee. This supports a context-matched risk pathway but does not show that repeated jumping alone causes a particular person’s pain.
context_requirements: Clinical examination is required to identify patellar tendinopathy.
missing_links: Direct tendon-load and within-person pain mediation were not measured.
uncertainty: Symptoms alone cannot identify this pathway.

hypotheses.title: Landing-load and local tissue-stress pathway
hypotheses.summary: Landing features predict estimated patellar-tendon loading. The transitions from estimated force to a local stress state and from stress to pain remain explicit model hypotheses.
context_requirements: Landing task and tissue context must be specified.
missing_links: No bundled study directly measures tendon force, tissue stress, nociceptive signaling, and pain in one causal chain.
hypotheses.evidence_label: Biomechanically plausible with weak downstream causal links

hypotheses.title: Competing patellofemoral mechanism family
hypotheses.summary: Force distribution and patellofemoral loading form a competing anatomical hypothesis. The bundled trial supports exercise plus education in an adolescent patellofemoral-pain population, not the proposed mechanical causal path.
context_requirements: Anterior-knee-pain phenotype and appropriate clinical context.
missing_links: The bundled study does not identify a specific mechanical cause.
hypotheses.evidence_label: Competing clinical branch with unvalidated mechanical links

interventions.name: Progressive tendon-loading rehabilitation concept
interventions.description: A staged program studied in clinically confirmed patellar tendinopathy. It is compared as a research class, not prescribed to an individual.
major_safety_concerns: Loading changes can aggravate symptoms and require context-appropriate professional guidance.
unsupported_assumptions: That the same program suits undifferentiated knee pain.

interventions.name: Training-load modification concept
interventions.description: A cause-oriented research concept motivated by an exposure–risk association; the pack supplies no universal safe threshold or personal schedule.
interventions.maturity: observational human evidence plus systems-model rationale
major_safety_concerns: Abrupt activity changes or prolonged inactivity can have consequences; no personal schedule is provided.

interventions.name: Isometric exercise for short-term pain response
interventions.description: A symptom-oriented exercise class with variable acute pain findings and no consistent superiority over isotonic exercise.
uncertainty: Responses vary within and across tendon conditions.
major_safety_concerns: Exercise selection and tolerance depend on clinical context.
unsupported_assumptions: Acute pain reduction implies tissue healing.

interventions.name: Education plus supervised exercise
interventions.description: A combined intervention studied in adolescents with patellofemoral pain; it belongs to a competing clinical branch.
major_safety_concerns: Requires context-appropriate exercise selection and symptom monitoring.
unsupported_assumptions: Generalization to patellar tendinopathy or all knee pain.

petri_model.name: Curated knee-load systems model
petri_model.description: A simplified educational model of repeated load, accumulated tissue stress, recovery, adaptation, an inflammatory-mediator state, pain sensitivity, and accumulated symptom output.

scenarios.label: Increase input
scenarios.description: Increase the synthetic mechanical input rate.

scenarios.label: Reduce input
scenarios.description: Reduce the synthetic mechanical input rate.

scenarios.label: Reduce recovery
scenarios.description: Lower the initial recovery state. Only crossing its gate changes recovery transition activity.

scenarios.label: Increase recovery
scenarios.description: Raise the initial recovery state. A gate already open need not increase downstream recovery.

scenarios.label: Increase input and reduce dissipation
scenarios.description: Increase synthetic input while reducing the dissipation rate.

assumptions: All places are dimensionless abstractions rather than patient measurements.
Recovery capacity and tissue stress are latent model constructs.
Pain is multifactorial; the model does not identify an anatomical diagnosis.
Synthetic rates support qualitative scenario comparisons only.

places.name: Accumulated tissue stress
places.description: Abstract accumulated stress, not tissue damage.

places.name: Recovery capacity
places.description: Latent recovery gate used for scenario comparison.

places.name: Adaptation
places.description: Abstract tissue adaptation that limits stress accumulation after reaching a threshold.

places.name: Inflammatory mediator state
places.description: Abstract mediator state, not an inferred biomarker.

places.name: Accumulated symptom output
places.description: Model output that is not a clinical pain prediction.

transitions.name: Mechanical load input
assumptions: Synthetic constant input; not a prescribed activity dose.

transitions.name: Stress accumulation
transitions.biological_event: Mechanical load contributes to an accumulated stress state.
assumptions: Stress is not damage and was not directly measured in the cited studies.

transitions.name: Stress recovery
transitions.biological_event: Stress clears when recovery capacity exceeds the declared gate.
assumptions: Recovery gate and rate are synthetic.

transitions.name: Adaptation formation
transitions.biological_event: Sustained loading contributes to a tissue-adaptation state.
assumptions: Gated qualitative approximation of chronic adaptation.

transitions.name: Adaptation decay
assumptions: Synthetic first-order loss; detraining was not estimated from the source.

transitions.name: Mediator activation
transitions.biological_event: Accumulated stress contributes to an inflammatory-mediator state.
assumptions: Unvalidated model bridge; no biomarker was measured by the cited review.

transitions.name: Pain-sensitivity activation
transitions.biological_event: Mediator state contributes to a pain-sensitivity state.
assumptions: Pain is not reducible to this state; qualitative bridge only.

transitions.name: Symptom-output accumulation
transitions.biological_event: Pain-sensitivity state adds to model symptom output.
assumptions: Output is not a clinical pain scale or personal prediction.
